records.exact_source_wording: Introducing building to stewardship on global sustainability, this study primarily tackles with direct application of the emergy evaluation as the practical principle at the early design phases.

A critical problem in introduction of emergy evaluation during the early design stages is its time-demanding calculation work and limited available data. So, establishment of a fast emergy analysis procedure and development of an easy-to-handle model was the essential task of this study, aiming at providing a logic for wider application of emergy analysis in practice. The proposed approach was clearly proved, and the final metamodel development provides an easily adaptable methodology for the building emergy simulation without a large numbers of tedious calculations.

For this study, a design development scenarios based on the reference building includes the building envelope and changes to the floor plan, i.e., length to width ratio. The fixed parameters are the floor area (A 1⁄4 1,660.5 m2), height (H 1⁄4 3.96 m) of each floor. Early building designers face questions mainly on (i) orientation, (ii) building shape, (iii) structure, and (iv) building envelope [24]. The design variables whose change have major influence in energy use and directly affect an exterior form include the length and width of floor, window size (W), building orientation (q), and wall insulation (M). Correlation of the plan length and width is regulated by the area, thus Area Ratio (AR) denotes the length divided by its width. Note that every variable is independent the other, and the variables of window and insulation are compartmentalized into four and two items respectively. To apply the L18 orthogonal array of Taguchi method for this case, each variable is divided into three different levels except for orientation. Angular measurement of orientation is on the azimuth basis, and it is set to be varied clockwise from zero to 90 . The window size varies individually within each elevation, and is represented by window-wall ratio. They are marked with the subscript S1, S2, S3, and S4 (WS1 ~ WS4).
